content.text:
We need to resolve March order from Winterfell (id region winterfell) with order March +0 (orderId 2). ActionGuidance lists reachable regions: castle-black (land, no castle), flints-finger (land, castleLevel 1), greywater-watch (land, castleLevel 0), karhold (land, no castle), moat-cailin (land, castleLevel 1), the-stony-shore (land, no castle), white-harbor (land, castleLevel 1). Also note that some trigger combat: greywater-watch triggers combat (has enemy units). Others no combat.

We must consider supply: Stark supply = 1. Currently Stark controls castle (Winterfell) and has units: winterfell has 1 knight (unit id 45). Also they have a ship at bay-of-ice (id 34), knight at castle-black (ids 2,28), knight at karhold (id 29). So total Stark units: 1 knight at Winterfell, 2 knights at Castle Black, 1 knight at Karhold, 1 ship at Bay of Ice. Supply 1 means allowed armies: per supply track 1 -> permitted army sizes: 3,2 (looking at table: 1 supply => 3,2). That means you can have up to two armies, one up to 3 units, one up to 2 units. Currently, how are armies defined? An army is two or more units in same area. Let's see:

- Castle Black: 2 knights -> that's an army of size 2.
- Karhold: 1 knight -> single unit, not an army.
- Winterfell: 1 knight -> single unit.
- Bay of Ice: 1 ship -> single unit.

Thus currently only one army (castle-black) size 2, which is within allowed (2). No other armies.

If we move the knight from Winterfell somewhere, we may create new army or join existing.

We cannot exceed supply: after moving, we must ensure armies count and sizes do not exceed allowed. Since we have supply 1, we can have up to two armies: size up to 3 and up to 2. So we could have at most two armies each >1 unit (or up to size). Single units are fine.

Potential moves:

- Move the knight to Flints-finger (enemy castle, currently controlled by Greyjoy, with no units). That would capture a castle (gain +1 castle area). No combat because there is no enemy unit there (but there is a castle, presumably unoccupied). Capturing empty area requires moving into empty area with no enemy units; you then control it (no combat). Need to place a control token? The rules: if you move into an area with no enemy units and no enemy power token, you take control automatically; you don't need a power token (you just occupy). So capture Flints-finger. That gives Stark a second castle area (now have Winterfell still? If we leave Winterfell empty, we must leave control token to keep Winterfell, but they said "no control token will be spent. These details are already settled." The note says: "Winterfell currently contributes 1 castle area to your score. Your existing control token or home symbol keeps this area yours when you leave it empty; no new token is needed." So we can vacate Winterfell without losing castle area. So moving knight away doesn't lose castle.

Thus after moving, Stark castles: Winterfell (still controlled), Flints-finger captured => total 2 castles.

- Move knight to Moat Cailin (enemy castle, controlled by Greyjoy). Same capture, no combat.

- Move knight to White Harbor (enemy castle, uncontrolled (no owner). capture.

- Could move to Castle Black, but already there is own army. Could move to Karhold (own area) join with knight there making an army of 2 at Karhold. That would be an army size 2, still okay. But no castle gain.

- Could move to The Stony Shore (no castle). No gain.

- Could move to Greywater-watch: there is enemy units (Greyjoy units). That would trigger combat. Might be significant: Greywater-watch has 1 footman, 2 knights (total 3 units). Stark would attack with 1 knight (maybe plus support). Need to check support around Greywater-watch. Let's see neighbors of Greywater-watch from map: neighbors: bay-of-ice, flints-finger, ironmans-bay, moat-cailin, seagard. Also it's a land area. Currently who has support orders adjacent? Revealed orders list: support orders at castle-black (Stark), karhold (Stark), bay-of-ice (Consolidate), the-reach (Lannister), oldtown (Lannister), etc. Support orders adjacent to Greywater-watch would be in any of its neighboring areas that have Support orders. Let's check each neighbor:

- bay-of-ice: order Consolidate Power (not support) => no support.
- flints-finger: no order (maybe not controlled?). In current revealed orders list, flints-finger not listed, so no order placed (cannot place order because must place order if unit present? Actually you must assign order to each area you control that has units. Flints-finger currently has no units, is controlled by Greyjoy but they have a castle, maybe they have no units, they would still need to assign order? The rule says: must place exactly one Order token on each area you control that contains at least one of your units. Since they have no units, they don't need to assign order. So no support.

- ironmans-bay: it's a sea area controlled by nobody (?) Actually ironmans-bay has no units; it's not a land area, but could have Support order? Support orders can be placed on any area containing units? Actually you can assign orders only on areas where you have at least one unit. So no support there.

- moat-cailin: is controlled by Greyjoy, has no units currently (in board units list, moat-cailin has no units). So no support there.

- seagard: controlled by Greyjoy. Units: none (but earlier they have no units). So no support.

Thus there is likely no support orders adjacent to Greywater-watch.

But also note: Lannister has a support at castle-black (Stark's support). That is not adjacent to Greywater-watch.

Thus attacking Greywater-watch would be a combat with likely 1 Stark knight vs 3 Greyjoy units. Stark's support maybe from Winterfell? Not allowed because support only from Support orders, not from units. So no support.

Could attack with just one knight, likely lose heavily.

Thus best move is capture a castle with no combat: Flints-finger, Moat Cailin, or White Harbor. Need to pick best considering supply.

Check supply safety: moving the knight from Winterfell makes Winterfell empty (no units). According to actionGuidance, "canLeavePowerToken": false, meaning they cannot leave a power token (but they said no control token will be spent, and we have home token or existing control token? Winterfell is home area of Stark, automatically controlled). So okay.

But also we must ensure that moving the knight to a destination doesn't cause supply violations.

Current armies after move:

Scenario: move knight to Flints-finger (occupied none). Then armies: Castle Black (size2), Flints-finger (size1 single unit) not an army, Karhold (size1), Bay of Ice (ship) size1. No new armies >1. So still only one army (castle-black). Supply fine.

If move to Moat Cailin (empty) similar.

If move to White Harbor (empty) similar.

If move to Karhold, we'd have Karhold with 2 knights => army size2. Then we would have two armies: Castle Black size2 and Karhold size2. Supply allowances: up to 2 armies; max sizes 3 and 2. Both size2, within max 2. So supply okay.

If move to The Stony Shore empty, similar.

Thus all options are supply-safe. Need consider strategic value: capturing additional castles increases victory points; currently Stark has 1 castle, 0 strongholds, 1 VP. Capturing more castles would help.

Which castles are currently controlled by other houses? Flints-finger (Greyjoy), Moat Cailin (Greyjoy), White Harbor (uncontrolled). Capturing White Harbor gives neutral castle, maybe less contested.

But also might affect supply icons? Castle capture may give supply icons later? Not immediate.

Potential to later support from new castle? Not now.

Thus best likely to capture an enemy castle: Flints-finger or Moat Cailin, but note they are adjacent to Greyjoy's territories, could be contested later.

Probably choose Flints-finger (castle, also reachable). Let's verify neighbor list includes Flints-finger.

Yes.

Thus our moves: move unit ID 45 (the knight) from Winterfell to flints-finger. The schema for moves only includes destination_region_id, not unit ids. The system will assume move all units? Actually we need to specify moves list, each entry only destination_region_id, not which units. But earlier schema: "moves": array of objects with destination_region_id. It seems they assume moving all eligible units? However we need to indicate which units. The description: "Destination groups and moving unit IDs... Unlisted units stay in source." But the schema only defines destination_region_id, no units list. Probably the system expects you to move all units from source to that destination (since only one unit type). Actually earlier similar tasks: they used moves with just destination ID, assuming moving entire army? Let's assume moving all units from source (since only one unit). That will move the single knight.

Thus final answer: moves:[{destination_region_id:"flints-finger"}]

Check the enum allowed: The enum list includes "flints-finger". Yes.

Thus output JSON.

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.

actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Before attacking another army, use check_neighbours on that battlefield to verify the supporting areas. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
